ios.desc:
Your world should read like a clock, not a spreadsheet.

Meridian is a clock-first world-time instrument for the places that matter to you. Instead of scanning unrelated clocks, see every saved city around one live 24-hour solar face. Daylight, local dates, and relative offsets stay visible together, so the shape of your world makes sense at a glance.

ONE FACE, EVERY CITY
• Focus any saved city with one tap.
• Read its local time, date, UTC offset, solar state, sunrise, and sunset.
• See every other city relative to the one in focus.
• Follow half-hour and quarter-hour time zones accurately.

CONVERT EXACT MOMENTS
With Meridian Plus, choose a date and time to see the matching local time and day in every saved city. Meridian follows the time-zone and daylight-saving rules carried by the operating system, including skipped and repeated local times. The last three moments you converted come back as one-tap rows. With Time Capture, paste a date, time, and city, review the details, and convert the confirmed moment across your saved clocks. Reviewing a captured time is free; applying it uses Plus or the Convert preview.

UPCOMING TIME CHANGES
See each saved city’s next clock change within 30 days and how its time difference from another saved city will change. Included free.

SOLAR ALERTS
With Meridian Plus, have sunrise, sunset, golden hour, blue hour, and solar noon announced for any saved city, on time or up to 30 minutes before.

WORLD ALARMS
With Meridian Plus on iOS and iPadOS 26 or later, set a one-time alarm for a saved city’s local date and time. See the matching time on your device before you enable it, or turn a future moment in Convert into an alarm. Open World Alarms from the alarm-clock button on the main screen. Alarms stay tied to the moment you confirmed, even when you travel.

YOUR CLOCKS EVERYWHERE
• iPhone and iPad layouts built for each screen.
• Focus, Constellation, Solar Atlas, and interactive Time Lens widgets.
• An extra-large iPad Solar Atlas for up to eight saved cities.
• Pin a city or follow your selected clock. Tap a widget to open its city.
• Choose a Time Lens comparison session in Edit Widget to step through time. Other clock widgets stay live.
• Lock Screen and StandBy views.
• Apple Watch app and complications.
• Private iCloud sync between your devices.

quotes.text:
That’s actually pretty close to what I ended up building.

For the first one, I skipped the map and went with search + saved cities instead. All your saved places sit on the same 24-hour dial, so you can see the difference from your local time at a glance without doing the timezone math. The upside is that it works completely offline and fits nicely on Apple Watch too.

Your second suggestion is the part I only got halfway right. You can move the dial in 15-minute increments and the daylight/twilight colouring changes with it. There’s also a calendar where you can jump to any date and time and see what the solar state is in every saved city, but right now that’s shown in rows rather than by recolouring the clock itself.

I like your version better though, hovering/scrubbing a time and having the whole clock recolour for that moment would make a lot more sense. I’m going to add that to the list.

I’m the developer, btw: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6797192832
